findings.title: Refusal of recognized truth and received good
findings.claim: Within the pericope's observation and reminder frame, the focus كَفَرَ can carry both refusal of recognized religious truth and covering the value of received benefit, so the exception describes a refusal that reaches truth and what has been given.
findings.mechanism: The objectless focus denial is contacted by the preceding camel observation and the immediate reminder and non-controller boundary. The trusted branch records distinguish denial of truth from ingratitude toward benefit, allowing the same refusal profile to be read against both kinds of received recognition without turning the two into one gloss.
findings.reader_payoff: The word translated as denial becomes more precise: the person has turned from an available field of recognition and can be seen both as refusing truth and as covering the good that called for acknowledgment.
findings.containment: The ordinary denial reading remains intact. This finding does not activate every covering branch, does not call another person an unbeliever, and does not claim that ingratitude replaces religious denial.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and trusted pericope connections directly supply the two target relations, while the cross-word synthesis from observation and reminder to the refusal remains a contextual inference.

findings.title: A turning-away inside directed sequence
findings.claim: The focus turning-away predicate stands inside the pericope's sequence of directed observation clauses and its closing return, so the refusal can be perceived as a bounded leg in movement that still has a destination.
findings.mechanism: The exact target surfaces repeat إلى across 88:17-20 and then give إلينا إيابهم at 88:25. Those independent directional and return cues contact the focus continuity facet of تَوَلَّىٰ and place its ordinary withdrawal within an ordered movement frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The clause no longer appears as an isolated refusal detached from what comes before and after: its turn sits within a movement that is directed, continues through the sequence, and closes toward return.
findings.containment: The ordinary meaning of turning away remains primary. This retains continuity pressure only; it does not make تَوَلَّىٰ mean taking possession, assert a separate return-branch carrier, or state a whole-surah architecture.

epistemic.reason: The focus continuity branch and exact target Arabic are supplied, but the movement-level connection is an inference and the target connection rows do not supply target morphology.

findings.title: Return and accounting close the attempted exit
findings.claim: The closing return and accounting turn the focus person's withdrawal into an outbound leg rather than an escape: return brings the person back toward the speaker's domain, and accounting preserves the relation after disavowal.
findings.mechanism: The attributed HFT trace joins the focus branches for turning away and rejecting a bond to the exact 88:25 return coordinate and the exact 88:26 accounting coordinate. The later return reverses apparent spatial exit, while the later account reverses the attempt to make disavowal dissolve the acts' relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The final clauses make the refusal's direction visible: turning away changes location in appearance, while the return and account keep the person and the acts within an answerable relation.
findings.containment: The ordinary readings of turning away, denial, return, and accounting remain recoverable. The accounting branch is retained only as the HFT-attributed role because its independent registry record is unresolved; the alternative remains that the closing clauses are general closure rather than a deliberate reversal of both focus predicates.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace supplies exact focus and context coordinates and explicit roles, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and the accounting root has no independent branch record in the packet.

findings.title: A covered load carried through departure and return
findings.claim: As a bounded material image, the focus covering word and its under-saddle layer can be heard with the camel and return anchors as a hidden load-bearing surface that carries pressure through departure and comes back with the traveler.
findings.mechanism: The attributed HFT trace contacts the focus w-l-y under-saddle branch and the focus k-f-r physical-covering branch with the exact 88:17 camel coordinate and 88:25 return coordinate. Covering hides the burden-bearing layer without removing pressure, while travel and return provide the route across which the hidden load persists.
findings.reader_payoff: The refusal clause can briefly disclose a material topology: what is covered may leave the eye while continuing to bear weight, and the journey does not make that pressure disappear.
findings.containment: This is exploratory and remote. The under-saddle branch cannot translate تَوَلَّىٰ, and the two context branches have no independent registry gloss; the image is retained only as an attributed material relation through the supplied focus cover, camel, and return coordinates. It does not say the person is literally camel equipment or replace the plain refusal reading.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace supplies exact coordinates and a contained changed reading, while the reader identity is legacy_unbound, the packet labels the outlier exploratory, and two context branch records remain unresolved.
